title: Residential sidewalk past a large tree (mock)

verdict.summary: Mostly a continuous sidewalk, but one slab beside the large tree (about 12 s in) is heaved enough to be a likely barrier for a wheelchair. Check its height before relying on this route.

findings.title: Heaved slab beside a tree trunk
findings.evidence_note: The slab next to the tree trunk is broken into several pieces that sit at different heights, with tree roots exposed along its outer edge. The raised edges look large enough to stop a front caster. Height is judged from video alone: verify on site.
findings.reference: 2010 ADA Standards 303.2-303.4: level changes over 1/4 in need a bevel; over 1/2 in, a ramp

findings.title: Cracked, tilted slab before the tree
findings.evidence_note: This slab is cracked across and its outer corner has dropped toward the dirt strip, leaving a cross-slope and an uneven joint. Passable with care; the slope is judged from video alone.
findings.reference: 2010 ADA Standards 303.2-303.4: level changes over 1/4 in need a bevel; over 1/2 in, a ramp

findings.title: Crack across a slab, possibly uneven
findings.evidence_note: SAM flagged this slab as raised. A crack runs across it, but on re-check the two sides look nearly flush. Kept at low confidence; verify on site.
findings.reference: 2010 ADA Standards 303.2-303.4: level changes over 1/4 in need a bevel; over 1/2 in, a ramp

checks.note: Trash bin seen at 1 s is beside the sidewalk, not on it.
No street crossing on this stretch.
No steps or ramp in this clip.
